en: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, both from 'Asim, with this chain of narration, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) concerning silk, the like of it.

Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, 'Asim al-Ahwal narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman, who said: 'Umar wrote to us while we were in Azerbaijan: "O 'Utbah ibn Farqad, it is not from your toil, nor from the toil of your father, nor from the toil of your mother; so satisfy the Muslims in their dwellings with what you satisfy yourself with in your dwelling. And beware of indulgence in luxury, the attire of the polytheists, and the wearing of silk, for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade wearing silk." He said: "Except like this," and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) raised his middle finger and index finger together for us. Zuhayr said: 'Asim said: "This was in the letter." He said: And Zuhayr raised his two fingers.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Ubayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Khalifah ibn Ka'b Abu Dhubyan, who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr delivering a sermon saying: "Behold, do not dress your women in silk, for I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Do not wear silk, for whoever wears it in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter.'"

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Khalid ibn 'Abdullah informed us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Abdullah, the freed slave of Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who was the maternal uncle of the children of 'Ata', saying: Asma' sent me to 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar saying: "It has reached me that you forbid three things: a silk border on a garment, the red-purple saddle-cushion (maytharah urjuwan), and fasting the entirety of Rajab." 'Abdullah said to me: "As for what you mentioned of Rajab, how about one who fasts continuously? As for what you mentioned of the silk border on a garment, I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'Only he wears silk who has no share [in the Hereafter],' so I feared that the border might be part of it. And as for the red-purple saddle-cushion, here is the saddle-cushion of 'Abdullah, and behold, it was red-purple." So I returned to Asma' and informed her, whereat she said: "Here is the cloak (jubbah) of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." She brought out to me a Persian cloak (tayalisah kisrawaniyyah) having a brocade collar-band and its two openings hemmed with brocade. She said: "This was with 'A'ishah until she passed away; when she passed away, I took possession of it. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to wear it, and we wash it for the sick so that healing is sought through it."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrating, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Salim ibn 'Abdullah said to me concerning istabraq: I said: "Whatever is thick and coarse of brocade." He said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar say: 'Umar saw a suit of istabraq on a man, so he brought it to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)... and he mentioned the like of their hadith, except that he said: So he said: "I only sent it to you so that you might obtain money through it."

Ibn Numayr narrated to me, Rawh narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Hafs narrated to us, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from his father, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab saw upon a man from the family of 'Utarid... with the like of the hadith of Yahya ibn Sa'id, except that he said: "I only sent it to you so that you might benefit from it, and I did not send it to you for you to wear it."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'bah, Abu Bakr ibn Hafs informed me, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, that 'Umar saw upon a man from the family of 'Utarid an outer gown (qaba') of brocade or silk, so he said to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "If only you bought it." He said: "Only he wears this who has no share [in the Hereafter]." Later, a silken-striped suit was gifted to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he sent it to me. He said: I said: "You sent it to me when I heard you say about it what you said?" He said: "I only sent it to you so that you might derive benefit from it."
Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Ibn Shihab, with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me—and the wording is that of Harmalah—they said: Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, Salim ibn 'Abdullah narrated to me that 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab found a suit of istabraq (heavy brocade) being sold in the market, so he took it and brought it to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, buy this and beautify yourself with it for the 'Eid and for delegations." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "This is only the clothing of one who has no share [in the Hereafter]." He said: 'Umar waited for as long as Allah willed. Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sent him a cloak of brocade. 'Umar brought it to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you said: 'This is only the clothing of one who has no share [in the Hereafter],' or 'Only he wears this who has no share,' and yet you sent this to me?" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "So that you may sell it and fulfill your need with it."

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, Nafi' narrated to us, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: 'Umar saw 'Utarid al-Tamimi displaying a silken-striped suit for sale in the market—and he was a man who used to visit kings and obtain gifts from them. 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw 'Utarid displaying a silken-striped suit in the market; would that you buy it and wear it for the Arab delegations when they come to you—and I think he also said: and wear it on Friday." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "Only he wears silk in this world who has no share in the Hereafter." After that, some silken-striped suits were brought to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so he sent a suit to 'Umar, a suit to Usamah ibn Zayd, and gave a suit to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, saying: "Tear it into head-coverings (khumur) among your womenfolk." He said: 'Umar came carrying his suit and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you sent this to me when yesterday you said concerning the suit of 'Utarid what you said?" He said: "I did not send it to you for you to wear it, but rather I sent it to you so that you might benefit from it." As for Usamah, he went out in the evening wearing his suit, so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) looked at him with a look by which Usamah knew that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) disapproved of what he had done. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, why do you look at me so, when you yourself sent it to me?" He replied: "I did not send it to you for you to wear it; rather, I sent it to you so that you might tear it into head-coverings among your womenfolk."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us; all of them from 'Ubaydullah; (H) and Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to me, Hafs ibn Maysarah narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah; both of them from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with something similar to the hadith of Malik.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab saw a silken-striped suit near the gate of the mosque and said: "O Messenger of Allah, would that you bought this and wore it for the people on Friday and for the delegations when they come to you." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Only he wears this who has no share in the Hereafter." Later, some of those suits came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he gave 'Umar a suit from them. 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, you clothed me with it when you said what you said concerning the suit of 'Utarid?" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "I did not clothe you with it for you to wear it." So 'Umar clothed a pagan brother of his in Mecca with it.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Sayf narrated to us, he said: I heard Mujahid saying: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla say: Hudhayfah asked for water, and a Magian gave him a drink in a silver vessel, whereat he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Do not wear silk or brocade, do not drink from vessels of gold and silver, and do not eat from their plates, for indeed they are for them in this world."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Jarir informed us, from Mansur; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, both from Mujahid, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with the meaning of the hadith of those whom we mentioned.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us, Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adiyy narrated to us; (H) and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr narrated to me, Bahz narrated to us; all of them from Shu'bah, with the like of the hadith of Mu'adh and his chain of narration; and none of them mentioned in the hadith: "I witnessed Hudhayfah," except Mu'adh alone; rather, they said: "Hudhayfah asked for water."

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, that he heard 'Abd al-Rahman—meaning Ibn Abi Layla—say: I witnessed Hudhayfah ask for water in al-Mada'in, and a person brought him a silver vessel... and he mentioned it with the meaning of the hadith of Ibn 'Ukaym from Hudhayfah.

'Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-'Ala' narrated to me, Sufyan narrated to us, Ibn Abi Najih narrated to us first from Mujahid, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Hudhayfah; then Yazid narrated to us that he heard it from Ibn Abi Layla, from Hudhayfah; then Abu Farwah narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn 'Ukaym—so I thought that Ibn Abi Layla only heard it from Ibn 'Ukaym—who said: We were with Hudhayfah in al-Mada'in... and he mentioned something similar to it, and did not say: "on the Day of Resurrection."

Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated it to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Farwah al-Juhani, who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Ukaym say: We were with Hudhayfah in al-Mada'in... and he mentioned something similar to it, and did not mention in the hadith: "on the Day of Resurrection."

Sa'id ibn 'Amr ibn Sahl ibn Ishaq ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ath ibn Qays narrated to us, he said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us—I heard him mentioning it—from Abu Farwah, that he heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Ukaym say: We were with Hudhayfah in al-Mada'in, and Hudhayfah asked for water. A village elder (dihqan) brought him a drink in a silver vessel, so he threw it at him and said: "I inform you that I had commanded him not to serve me drink in it, for the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Do not drink from vessels of gold and silver, and do not wear brocade and silk, for they are for them in this world and for you in the Hereafter on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Yahya ibn Adam and 'Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, they said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha', with their chain of narration, and he said: "and spreading salam, and a gold ring," without doubt.

Abu Kurayb narrated it to us, Ibn Idris narrated to us, Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani and Layth ibn Abi Sulaym informed us, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha', with their chain of narration, and did not mention the addition of Jarir and Ibn Mushir; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us; (H) and 'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi informed us; (H) and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr narrated to us, Bahz narrated to us; all of them said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn Sulaym, with their chain of narration and the meaning of their hadith, except for his words "and spreading salam," for he said in place of it: "and returning salam," and he said: "he forbade us from a gold ring or a gold band."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us; (H) and 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, both from al-Shaybani, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha', with this chain of narration, similar to the hadith of Zuhayr; and he said: "helping fulfill the oath," without doubt; and he added in the hadith: "and from drinking in silver vessels, for whoever drinks from them in this world will not drink from them in the Hereafter."

Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn Sulaym, with this chain of narration, the like of it, except for his words: "and helping fulfill the oath or the swearing person," for he did not mention this phrase in the hadith, and in its place put: "and announcing a lost animal."

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi narrated to us, Abu Khaythamah informed us, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha'; (H) and Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Ash'ath narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Suwayd ibn Muqarrin narrated to me, saying: I entered upon al-Bara' ibn 'Azib and heard him say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commanded us with seven and forbade us from seven. He commanded us to visit the sick, follow the funeral procession, invoke Allah's mercy on the one who sneezes, help fulfill the oath (or the one who swears), help the wronged, accept invitations, and spread salam. And he forbade us from wearing gold rings, drinking from silver vessels, using mayathir cushions, wearing al-qassi garments, and wearing ordinary silk, istabraq (heavy brocade), and dibaj (pure silk brocade).

Zayd ibn Yazid Abu Ma'n al-Raqashi narrated to me, Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Uthman—meaning Ibn Murrah—'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from his maternal aunt Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever drinks from a vessel of gold or silver only churns into his belly fire from Hell."

Qutaybah and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated it to us, from al-Layth ibn Sa'd; (H) and 'Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di narrated it to me, Isma'il—meaning Ibn 'Ulayyah—narrated to us, from Ayyub; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Walid ibn Shuja' narrated to us, they said: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah; (H) and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami narrated to us, al-Fudayl ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Uqbah narrated to us; (H) and Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, Jarir—meaning Ibn Hazim—narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sarraj; all of them from Nafi', with the like of the hadith of Malik ibn Anas with his chain of narration from Nafi'; and he added in the hadith of 'Ali ibn Mushir from 'Ubaydullah: "Indeed, the one who eats or drinks from vessels of silver and gold..." and there is not in the hadith of any of them mention of eating and gold except in the hadith of Ibn Mushir.

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Nafi', from Zayd ibn 'Abdullah, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, from Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The one who drinks from silver vessels only churns into his belly the fire of Hell."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and 'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Kurayb's—they said: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Yahya the freed slave of the family of Ja'dah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I never saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) criticize food ever; if he had an appetite for it he ate it, and if he did not care for it he kept silent. And Abu Kurayb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us, they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with the like of it.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr, and 'Umar ibn Sa'd Abu Dawud al-Hafari informed us, all of them from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, with this chain of narration, something similar to it.
Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Sulayman al-A'mash narrated to us, with this chain of narration, the like of it.
